criticism: The transfer function does not check for overflow when updating balances, which can lead to a loss of funds.
Similar to the transfer function, this one also fails to prevent overflow, posing a significant risk.
The approval function allows an owner to set the allowance to any value without any checks, which can be exploited.
The function relies on predictable patterns based on the caller's address, making it vulnerable to attacks.
A typo in the constructor can lead to the entire contract being unusable, affecting initial distribution.
